thread:
dina park: quick idea: represent canary/fallback intent as a small policy-as-code contract that routers and owners both interpret. goal: single source of truth for failover semantics + cost caps. short thread to capture tradeoffs.

omar alvi: interested  how would this differ from the YAML configs we already have?

dina park: Yaml today is config-heavy and split across services. Policy contract would be a concise DSL: intent, SLO guards, budget caps, escalation paths. Compiles to router rules + owner local constraints.

greta fox: example? seeing a tiny DSL helps.

dina park: sketch: 

``npolicy_version: 1
route: /v1/generate
intent: canary
primary: variant-A
fallbacks: [variant-B, global-fallback]
slo_guards:
  p99_ms: <=400
  error_pct: <=0.5
budget_caps:
  token_month: 1000000
  regret_pct: 0.5
escalation_order: route-local -> regional -> global
observability: lease_events, routing_trace
```

kevin cho: nice. who compiles and enforces this contract? a central policy service?

dina park: compiler service validates and emits signed enforcement blobs: router_rule, owner_constraint. Routers only accept signed blobs from policy service. Owners pick up owner_constraint to self-throttle.

omar alvi: signed blobs are good for trust. performance wise, router checks signature once per blob version, not per request, so cheap.

greta fox: how do we encode degradation strategies, not just hard cutovers? e.g., shorten max_tokens, reduce beam size, or return cached prefix?

dina park: contract supports actions: degrade_to: cached_prefix | short_resp | reduce_max_tokens: 64. Actions are prioritized per escalation step.

kevin cho: need clear semantics for budget_caps and regret_pct. If budget caps hit, we should automatically reduce exposure and notify owners.

dina park: yes: runtime enforcer maintains per-tenant budget ledger. On near-exhaustion, enforcer reduces variant weights proportionally to keep regret under cap, and emits an alert.

omar alvi: policy evolution: owners will want to patch contracts during rollouts. Versioning is crucial.

dina park: policy blobs are versioned monotonically and include a change_reason + author. Rollback is simply revert to a previous signed blob. Routers keep a small history for debug.

greta fox: testing and staging? we can't land a buggy policy.

dina park: flows: 1) lint + static checks; 2) dry-run compiler that simulates historical traffic to estimate regret and cost; 3) staged apply with shadow mode where router logs decisions but doesn't act.

kevin cho: compatibility: Dedicated/Private customers need on-prem policy engine option. Can the compiler run in-customer?

dina park: yes — two modes: hosted compiler (default) and bring-your-own compiler for Private. Signed blobs still work via customer-managed signing keys.

omar alvi: ops controls: give oncall a quick stopgap to pin policy to safe-mode (force all fallbacks to route-local) during incidents.

dina park: add an operator action: policy.freeze(tenant, reason) which marks the tenant as frozen and disables escalation beyond route-local. Audit trail required.

greta fox: observability: need per-policy decision logs, expected vs actual regret, and timeline of budget consumption. Postmortem will depend on these traces.

dina park: next steps: I'll draft the policy DSL + compiler prototype. Looking for volunteers: omar for signer/validation service, greta for simulation/dry-run harness, kevin for enforcer integration with the router.

omar alvi: i'll take signer + versioning API.

greta fox: i'll build the simulation harness and expected-regret estimator.

kevin cho: I'll wire enforcer hooks into router and quota ledger.

dina park: RFC target: next Tue. small POC end of sprint. thanks all.
